summary: The sequential channel latches terminalError under lifecycleSync and rejects later Exchange calls. createMultiplexed has no equivalent terminal/disposal guard: its receive loop faults the waiters present at termination, but a later Exchange can register a new waiter, complete Send and await forever when receive has already settled. The repository's ManualTransport demonstrates that Send may legally remain successful after CompleteReceive/disposal, so relying on the transport to reject late calls is insufficient at this seam. Existing cited tests explicitly check late admission/idempotent disposal for Sequential and only receive-enumerator settlement for Multiplexed. This is a source-derived lifecycle/counterexample question, not an executed CLR reproduction; reproduce with the existing inert transport and qualify both correlation strategies before claiming a family-wide closure guarantee.
title: Multiplexed channel lacks the sequential terminal-admission fence
